theories.claim: Manual ultraplan.yml line parser in internal/platform/config silently diverges from standard YAML writers, causing effective config to retain defaults while file appears valid
theories.basis: internal/platform/config/config.go:197-269 implements loadFile with bufio.Scanner, leadingWhitespace, string prefix checks for sections/lists, strings.SplitN(line,":",2) and single-quote stripping at :250, :226. It only handles list fields enumerated in listConfigField() at :553 and clears lists via clearListField(). Quoted values containing ':' , inline/bracket YAML, or indentation variations would be mis-split or rejected, while Validate() at :425 would still pass because defaults remain. internal/app/config_commands.go:37-40 surfaces effective config without surfacing parse truncation.
theories.verification_surface: static review of loadFile parser vs any writer of ultraplan.yml (platform/config writer, tests, or user edits) and static check of error paths for unsupported line at :248
theories.confirmation_condition: a well-formed ultraplan.yml emitted by a YAML marshaller (e.g., value "host:8080" or flow list) is parsed with truncated value, dropped list items, or "unsupported line" error while Validate passes on retained defaults, demonstrating writer/reader contract break
theories.refutation_condition: loadFile is the sole writer/reader and all workspace files are always produced/validated through this exact parser, with tests and validation rejecting any standard-YAML form that the parser cannot handle, so no drift occurs
theories.inconclusive_condition: cannot execute parser with fixtures or inspect writer implementation without approved check or context expansion; read-only static review alone cannot prove runtime drift
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: read-only parse of config.go:197-269 and config_commands.go:33-41; compare listConfigField allowlist and SplitN logic against expected YAML; no execution or file creation
